title: Citizen Kane
tagline: The classic story of power and the press.
about: A reporter chases the meaning of a newspaper king's last word, Rosebud, through the people who knew him.

    Early editionDeclaration of Principles oysters RockefellerKane's Declaration of Principles. Baked oysters under buttery greens and crumbs.How to make it24 oysters in the half shell100g butter, softened2 spring onions, chopped1 cup baby spinach1/2 cup flat-leaf parsley1/2 tsp fennel seeds, crushed40g fine breadcrumbs30g parmesan, finely grated1 lemon, in wedges2 cups rock saltBlitz the butter, spring onions, spinach, parsley and fennel to a green paste and season.Spread the rock salt on a tray and nestle the oysters in it.Top each oyster with a spoon of green butter, then the crumbs mixed with parmesan.Bake at 230°C until bubbling and golden, and serve with lemon.Everglades picnic fried chickenThe fight in the tent at the picnic. Buttermilk fried chicken with honey hot sauce.How to make it800g chicken thigh fillets, halved300ml buttermilk150g plain flour2 tsp sweet paprika1 tsp garlic powder1 L vegetable oil, for frying3 tbsp honey2 tbsp TabascoSoak the chicken in the buttermilk with a big pinch of salt.Mix the flour with the paprika, garlic powder and pepper, and dredge the chicken well.Fry in oil at 170°C in batches until deep golden and cooked through.Warm the honey with the Tabasco and drizzle over the hot chicken.A bag of hot salted peanutsSomebody will write a song about it.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Front pageWelcome-to-the-Inquirer roast sirloinKane hires the Chronicle's best men. Rare roast sirloin with Yorkshire puddings.How to make it1.5kg beef sirloin roast2 tbsp olive oil2 tbsp hot English mustard140g plain flour4 eggs200ml milk4 tbsp beef dripping or vegetable oil2 tbsp horseradish creamRub the beef with oil, salt and pepper and roast at 220°C, then turn down to 180°C until rare in the middle.Brush with the mustard and rest under foil.Whisk the flour, eggs and milk to a smooth batter.Heat the dripping in a muffin tray at 230°C, pour in the batter and bake until tall and crisp.Carve the beef thinly and serve with the puddings and horseradish.Still-hungry lobster NewburgLeland asks if Kane is still eating. Lobster in a paprika cream sauce on buttered toast.How to make it500g cooked lobster meat, in chunks50g butter1 lemon, juiced300ml thickened cream3 egg yolks1/4 tsp cayenne pepper1/2 tsp sweet paprika4 thick slices of white bread1 tbsp chives, snippedWarm the lobster gently in the butter, then add the lemon juice.Whisk the cream with the yolks, pour in and stir over low heat until it coats a spoon.Season with the cayenne, paprika and salt.Toast and butter the bread, spoon over the lobster and finish with chives.Sweet stuffRosebud snowfall pavlovaKane's last word was Rosebud. Snowy meringue piled with raspberries and cream.How to make it4 egg whites220g caster sugar1 tsp cornflour1 tsp white vinegar300ml thickened cream250g raspberries2 tbsp icing sugarWhisk the egg whites to soft peaks, then add the sugar a spoon at a time until thick and glossy.Fold in the cornflour and vinegar and pile into a round on a lined tray.Bake at 120°C, then turn off the oven and let it cool inside.Whip the cream, spread over the top, pile on the raspberries and dust with icing sugar like snow.Late extraSusan's nightclub highballSusan won't talk to the reporter. Rye whiskey and ginger beer with lemon peel.How to make it240ml rye whiskey800ml ginger beer, chilled1 lemon2 cups ice cubesFill 4 highball glasses with ice and add 60ml rye to each.Top with ginger beer and twist a strip of lemon peel over each.Iced champagne for the new staffFor the men who came over from the Chronicle.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
